predecessors.name: Peiligang culture
predecessors.text: the Peiligang country of Xinzheng and the Yi-Luo basin

predecessors.name: Cishan culture
predecessors.text: the Cishan country of southern Hebei and northern Henan, without the Shandong cells of the disc

predecessors.name: Dadiwan culture
predecessors.text: Gansu: "Dadiwan sites in the Wei River valley"; museum caption "Gansu Province, Neolithic period, Yangshao culture"; the western branch becomes Majiayao

successors.name: Longshan Culture
successors.text: the Yangshao culture area 3300-3000 BCE: the Wei valley, Shanxi, Henan and southern Hebei, without the Majiayao country in Gansu

successors.name: Majiayao culture
successors.text: Gansu: "Dadiwan sites in the Wei River valley"; museum caption "Gansu Province, Neolithic period, Yangshao culture"; the western branch becomes Majiayao

ledger.x: 5000 BCE: the Yangshao culture begins in the Wei valley and Shanxi: "from around 5000 BC to 3000 BC", "The Early Yangshao period or Banpo phase (c.

5000 BCE: the Yangshao takes the Peiligang country; infobox "Preceded by: Peiligang, Cishan, Dadiwan, and Baijia cultures"; Yangshao harvesting knives were "replacing earlier stone sickles found in the Peiligang and Cishan cultures".
5000 BCE: the Yangshao takes the Cishan country of southern Hebei and northern Henan.
5000 BCE: the rest of Henan, where "The culture flourished mainly in Henan" (Shuanghuaishu, the type region); no earlier state is named for it.

5000 BCE: the western Wei valley in Gansu, where the Dadiwan culture preceded the Yangshao; the Yangshao page names no date for the Dadiwan and the Dadiwan page says only that "The Yangshao follows Dadiwan in the local sequence", so the year is a bridge and the land passes through…
4000 BCE: the Middle Yangshao, the Miaodigou phase, begins: "The Middle Yangshao period or Miaodigou phase (c.
3500 BCE: the Late Yangshao begins: "The Late Yangshao period (c.
3300 BCE: the western branch becomes the Majiayao culture in Gansu: infobox "Followed by: Majiayao (3300-2000 BC)"; the page calls the Majiayao "its western branch".

3000 BCE: the Yangshao gives way to the Longshan culture ("3000-1900 BC"); the page says "Unlike the later Longshan culture, the Yangshao culture did not use pottery wheels" and calls the Shandong Longshan "its eastern branch".

certainty.note: The culture is known from village sites; the page gives no frontier, so every edge is soft.
